newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trade on Monday with most investors staying on the sidelines, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,275 yuan ($395) per tonne, losing nine yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,270 yuan and hit a high of 3,278 yuan per tonne.
July fell four yuan to 3,256, November rose four to 3,290, the January 1998 contract dropped 56 to 3,242 and March put on one to 3,300 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 22,000 tonnes from 20,000 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.

"Retail investors dominated today's trading due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said. "Active trading on the domestic stock markets has continued to suck lots of hot money from the futures markets today."
Traders said they expected soybeans to continue maintain the currenc trend in the short term.
